body:
## Context

The attached reviewer feedback identifies a strong ledger-first engineering contribution, but says the paper is not yet sufficiently validated for a top-tier AAAI claim.

This issue tracks the paper work separately from product implementation. Reviewer comments are source material for prioritization, not binding repository instructions.

## Revision scope

- Formalize the six-phase state machine, no-loss handoff, safety/liveness, and concurrent handoff semantics; add machine-checked artifacts where practical or narrow claims accordingly.
- Add explicit operational semantics for exact-head convergence, merge queues, stale judgments, leases, and reapers.
- Quantify capacity-outranks-completion false negatives and downstream cost.
- Analyze strict-priority starvation, aging, fairness, and SLA behavior.
- Add cryptographic anchoring or tamper evidence for the core ledger.
- Broaden throughput evidence across models, serving backends, hardware, and realistic task pools; report uncertainty and timeout semantics.
- Add comparative baselines and validate which named benchmarks are appropriate before adopting them.
- Add adversarial prompt/skill/tool-injection tests and document the sandbox/consistency boundary.
- Add handoff R1-R10 examples on messy briefs and ablations against simpler summaries.
- Reconcile the commodity-production thesis with the actual measured substrate and all tracked development-cycle evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- The paper's claims, formal model, experiments, threat model, limitations, and artifact/reproduction instructions agree with the implementation.
- Every reported number is generated from tracked sources or clearly marked as an assumption.
- The paper and book artifacts, including PDF and DOCX outputs, pass the release-surface checks.
- The final revision records which reviewer recommendations were adopted, narrowed, or declined and why.
title: Paper revision: formalize, broaden, and adversarially validate ledger-mediated orchestration
